Shark tunnel | A shark tunnel (or aquarium tunnel or acrylic tunnel or exhibit tunnel) is an underwater tunnel that passes through an aquarium, typically with sharks and related aquatic life.
Washburn Tunnel | The Washburn Tunnel is a two-lane underwater motor-vehicle tunnel connecting Galena Park and Pasadena, two suburbs of Houston, Texas.  Completed in 1950, it travels north-south underneath the Houston Ship Channel.  It was named after Harris County, Texas Auditor Harry L. Washburn.  It is the largest and first toll-free vehicular tunnel in the Southern United States.

Stateline Country Club | The Stateline Country Club, just inside the state border in what is now Stateline, Nevada, started as a small cafe.  Inside, visitors enjoying the early 1930s at Lake Tahoe could find a soda fountain bar and a few tables to enjoy a meal.  There was a small room in the rear where a poker game started-up most nights, and next door there was provision for vacationers at Carl F. Tychsen's Stateline Market with a pair of gas pumps nearby.
Pershing County, Nevada | Pershing County is a county in the U.S. state of Nevada.  As of the 2010 census, the population was 6,753.  Its county seat is Lovelock.  The county was named after army general John J. Pershing (1860–1948).  It was formed from Humboldt County in 1919, and the last county to be established in Nevada.  The Black Rock Desert, location for the annual Burning Man festival, is partially in the county.
